exposure: Ventricular subgaleal shunt (VSGS) technique for hydrocephalus
outcome: Death within the first year of life
Ability to walk at 2 years old
Presence of cerebral palsy at 2 years old
Need for special education assistance at 6 years old
cohort: The study included 32 children less than three months old with hydrocephalus who were treated by VSGS at Rouen University Hospital between January 2013 and December 2023.
finding: The study found that 75% of patients required definitive shunting, 45% acquired the ability to walk and had cerebral palsy by age 2, and 40% of those over 6 years old required special educational needs, with a 13.6% mortality rate within the first year.
